decision.keyword_policy: Exercise standard JSON Schema generation for tested 2020-12 shapes. Fail clearly for unsupported assertion keywords rather than silently weakening constraints. x-* are annotations; apply explicit model strategies for native range/binding meaning. Revalidate final overlaid values with a prepared validator and retain server validation as authority.
decision.optional_value_provider: One bounded Node JSONSchemaFaker subprocess per schema batch; provider is replaceable by an ordinary Python callback and is not required when explicit strategies supply values.
decision.orchestration: Python population core and existing tools/client.py

provider_bounds.processes: one per bounded batch; no persistent worker

decision.receipt_binding: Require response.status=committed, response.result.kind=records, nested response.result.result.operation_id equal to the exact saved plan request operation_id, and exact proposal/plan request equality. Unknown outcomes retain the original plan/context and block progress.
decision.state_boundary: Caller-owned state retains accepted pools/counts/usage, explicit attempt cursor, one pending proposal and exact saved plan; proposals do not publish parents or fulfill quotas. Only a matching committed records receipt advances accepted state.

git_delivery.future_pushes: ordinary main pushes; never overwrite unexpected new upstream commits
git_delivery.result: exact force-with-lease push succeeded; origin now has linear verified G8 history

commands: BIN=/tmp/rebase-g84-redb-payload/rebase-next-0.16.0-linux-x86_64-redb/bin/rebase-next; for m in calculation equipment invoicing measurement effect-demo quantity; do $BIN --model $m model public > /tmp/g90-native/$m.public.json; $BIN --model $m model developer > /tmp/g90-native/$m.developer.json; done
limitations: CLI native validation is schema/native binding validation, not a transaction or aggregate proof.

Equipment available_before alone does not prove arbitrary interval feasibility; the accepted recipe must use increasing starts, a common future end and no unseen intermediate capacity loss, or an explicit whole-interval rule.
Public HTTP catalog omits reference declarations; trusted developer catalog contains references and private contracts, so population must select public contracts and use declared target metadata.
Generated proposals are not committed parents; server authority, OCC, global invariants and aggregate feasibility remain authoritative.
The provider timing is value generation only and does not establish end-to-end throughput.
